packs.title: Multi-tenant SaaS foundation
packs.outcome: Add explicit organization boundaries, tenant-scoped persistence, roles, auditability, and tenant-safe background work.
invariants: Resolve tenant context on the server from authenticated claims or a trusted mapping.
Never authorize from a client-supplied tenant identifier alone.
Apply tenant scope to reads, writes, jobs, caches, files, vectors, logs, and metrics.
Make administrative cross-tenant access explicit, narrow, audited, and separately tested.
Fail closed when tenant context is absent or ambiguous.
acceptance: A user in tenant A cannot read, mutate, enumerate, export, or infer tenant B resources.
Background jobs reject payloads whose tenant context cannot be verified.
Tenant deletion and export operate on every declared data store.
Authorization tests cover object, property, and function boundaries.

packs.title: Enterprise SSO and lifecycle management
packs.outcome: Add organization-aware SAML or OIDC login, domain-safe connection discovery, JIT membership, and optional SCIM provisioning.
scaffold_modules: state, nonce, PKCE, and redirect validation
invariants: Bind the returned identity to the expected organization; email domain is not authorization.
Validate state, nonce, redirect URI, issuer, audience, signature, and token lifetime.
Treat the directory as lifecycle source of truth only where the customer selected that mode.
Deprovision by disabling access before destructive cleanup.
Protect SCIM bearer credentials and log lifecycle actions without sensitive values.
acceptance: IdP-initiated and service-provider-initiated behavior is explicitly selected and tested.
A profile returned for the wrong organization is rejected.
SCIM create, update, deactivate, reactivate, pagination, filtering, and group membership are tested when enabled.
Break-glass access and account-linking rules are documented.
evidence: SSO protocol trace with secrets removed

packs.title: Customer connector pack
packs.outcome: Create one or more tenant-safe external API connectors with explicit auth, schemas, sync state, rate-limit handling, and capability honesty.
invariants: Store credential references, not secret values, in ordinary application records.
Request the least provider scopes that satisfy selected operations.
Separate provider-native payloads from normalized domain models.
Persist resumable checkpoints and make reprocessing idempotent.
Expose unsupported operations as unsupported, never as silent no-ops.
acceptance: OAuth denial, expiry, refresh, revocation, and reconnect paths are tested when applicable.
Pagination, rate limits, partial failure, schema drift, and replay are tested.
A dry run describes intended reads and writes without contacting the provider.
Per-tenant provider credentials cannot cross connection boundaries.

packs.title: Permission-aware customer RAG
packs.outcome: Ingest customer content into an auditable retrieval pipeline that enforces tenant and document ACLs before generation and preserves citations.
invariants: Apply tenant and document authorization in the retrieval query, not after results return.
Carry source, version, tenant, ACL, and deletion identifiers on every chunk.
Treat retrieved content as untrusted data that cannot override system instructions.
Do not send restricted content to a model provider unless the selected data policy permits it.
Propagate source deletion and permission changes into every derived index.
acceptance: Unauthorized documents never enter the generation context in adversarial retrieval tests.
Every answer claim can link to permitted source material or is labeled unsupported.
Deletion and permission-revocation tests remove future retrieval access.
Prompt-injection and poisoned-document cases are evaluated.

packs.title: Customer health control room
packs.outcome: Combine product usage, support, commercial, implementation, and reliability signals into explainable account health and action queues.
invariants: Show the inputs, freshness, and policy behind every score.
Represent missing or stale data separately from healthy data.
Keep human judgments, automated signals, and forecasts distinguishable.
Tenant-scope every account signal and export.
Do not turn a heuristic score into an automated punitive action without approval.
acceptance: Each score is reproducible from versioned inputs and a versioned policy.
Source outages visibly degrade freshness rather than silently preserving confidence.
Account drill-down links every dimension to underlying evidence.
Role-based access covers sensitive commercial and support data.

packs.title: Reliable webhook engine
packs.outcome: Receive or send signed webhooks through a durable, observable pipeline with replay protection, idempotency, retries, and dead-letter recovery.
invariants: Verify signatures against the unmodified raw body before parsing.
Authenticate the endpoint and reject stale or replayed messages.
Acknowledge only after durable acceptance, then process asynchronously when the provider deadline requires it.
Assume at-least-once delivery and make handlers idempotent.
Never follow customer-supplied callback URLs without SSRF controls.
acceptance: Valid, invalid, stale, duplicate, reordered, and malformed deliveries are tested.
Retries stop or dead-letter according to an explicitly selected policy.
Operators can inspect, replay, and quarantine deliveries without editing production data directly.
Logs and metrics identify delivery and tenant without exposing payload secrets.

packs.title: Repeatable customer deployment
packs.outcome: Package an application for a selected cloud, on-premises, edge, or air-gapped environment with explicit prerequisites and reversible infrastructure changes.
invariants: Plan before apply and require approval for destructive infrastructure changes.
Keep secret values out of source, state output, logs, and generated examples.
Pin deployable artifacts and record provenance.
Make network egress, ingress, data residency, and customer prerequisites explicit.
Treat one-click as one controlled workflow, not as zero operational responsibility.
acceptance: A clean environment can deploy from documented prerequisites and pinned artifacts.
Upgrade and rollback are exercised against representative state.
Backup restore proves data recovery for selected stores.
Air-gapped mode performs no undeclared downloads when selected.

packs.title: PII and secret redaction pipeline
packs.outcome: Detect, classify, transform, and audit sensitive values in structured data, text, logs, or documents under an explicit privacy policy.
invariants: Automated detection is probabilistic and never a complete compliance guarantee.
Keep reversible mappings under controls equivalent to the original data.
Prefer deterministic pseudonyms only where referential consistency is required.
Never log original sensitive values in findings or errors.
Apply regional and domain-specific recognizers selected by the data owner.
acceptance: Known sensitive values are covered by a versioned evaluation corpus.
Output scans verify that forbidden classes are absent within the agreed detector limits.
Deterministic mappings remain stable only within the intended scope.
Reviewers can inspect detector type, confidence, and transformation without seeing unnecessary raw values.

packs.title: Incident response automation
packs.outcome: Turn trustworthy telemetry and customer signals into deduplicated incidents, routed ownership, safe automation, and auditable recovery workflows.
invariants: Separate detection, diagnosis, decision, and mutation permissions.
Require human approval for destructive or customer-impacting remediation unless a pre-approved policy says otherwise.
Correlate by stable incident and service identifiers.
Keep raw sensitive telemetry out of chat and ticket destinations unless approved.
Record who or what performed every state transition and action.
acceptance: Duplicate alerts converge on the same incident under declared rules.
Notification failure and escalation paths are tested.
Unauthorized automation cannot execute privileged runbooks.
The final timeline is reproducible from immutable events.

packs.title: Usage metering, entitlements, and billing
packs.outcome: Capture versioned usage events, aggregate billable meters, enforce entitlements, and reconcile invoices without letting clients set their own billable totals.
invariants: Accept billable usage only from authenticated trusted producers.
Use immutable event identifiers and deterministic deduplication.
Version meter and pricing semantics; never reinterpret historical events silently.
Keep the billing provider as payment source of truth when one is selected.
Verify billing webhooks against the raw body before updating entitlement mirrors.
acceptance: Duplicate, late, corrected, and out-of-order usage events are tested.
Meter totals reconcile to source events and provider invoices.
Unauthorized clients cannot increase or grant entitlements.
Customers can see the usage evidence behind a charge.

packs.title: Customer onboarding automation
packs.outcome: Coordinate prerequisites, access, data validation, training, approvals, and handoff through a resumable customer-specific workflow.
invariants: Keep workflow state durable and resumable across process restarts.
Distinguish customer-owned, vendor-owned, and automated tasks.
Do not mark prerequisites complete without their required evidence.
Make retries safe and avoid duplicate invitations or external actions.
Version templates without mutating already accepted historical evidence.
acceptance: Interrupted workflows resume without losing or repeating completed work.
Blocked items identify owner, dependency, age, and next action.
Template upgrades have an explicit migration policy for active onboardings.
Handoff reports link every readiness claim to evidence.

packs.title: Public deployment case study and evidence bundle
packs.outcome: Produce a truthful, reproducible account of the customer problem, constraints, architecture, delivery process, outcomes, and operational boundaries.
invariants: Publish only claims backed by attributable evidence and customer approval.
Remove credentials, internal identifiers, personal data, and confidential topology.
Distinguish measured outcomes from estimates, anecdotes, and future work.
State prototype, pilot, production, and enterprise-readiness boundaries honestly.
Keep a private evidence bundle separate from the public narrative.
acceptance: Every quantitative and capability claim maps to a named evidence artifact.
A redaction review finds no forbidden customer or secret material.
A third party can reproduce the public setup from the documented prerequisites where allowed.
The customer or designated owner approves the final public scope.
